audited_revision.name: QuantEngine_PHASE158_RELEASE_CANDIDATE.zip
audited_revision.superseded_by: revision 2 (this tree). The revision-1 identity (sha256, member count, byte count) is recorded in PHASE158_AUDIT_DISPOSITION.json in the post-build bundle and beside the superseded archive in _phase158_audited/. audited_revision.report: PHASE158_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT_FINDINGS.json as delivered by the operator (kept beside the superseded archive in _phase158_audited/; it audits revision 1, so it does not ship inside revision 2). The items below quote the findings as reported.
audited_revision.audit_environment: Linux, Python 3.13.5 (reported); the recorded build environment is Windows-10-10.0.19045-SP0 / Python 3.12.10. The auditor held the ZIP alone (no detached record, no post-build bundle, no input archive), which limited what items 1, 13 and 16 could establish; that is a handoff limitation recorded here, not an archive defect.

findings_requiring_action.as_reported: raw venue order ids appear in sealed historical records under reports/ and research/results/, which the audit read against the prompt's strict no-order-id condition for those roots; and a green PRIVACY_SCAN_PASS could be read as publication clearance.
findings_requiring_action.verified: reproduced. The scanner counts 38 raw venue order ids across the raw captures; the historical baseline is 13 sealed records (byte-identical to their input-archive members, never rewritten); new leakage is 0.
findings_requiring_action.disposition: the policy is stated, not relaxed. The enforced rule is: no raw order id may appear in reports/, docs/ or research/results/ EXCEPT in a file byte-identical to its input-archive member (the enumerated historical baseline); any new or modified carrier fails the scan. The revision-1 prompt's wording omitted the exception, and that was the imprecision F-01 exposed. The prompt, the privacy review and the scanner now all state the rule and the package class together; the scan report carries publication_clearance=NOT_CLEARED with a reason, and tests/test_phase158_privacy_contract.py pins it. The archive remains a restricted evidence package and is NOT cleared for publication.

findings_requiring_action.as_reported: a targeted test run left the worktree manifest-invalid: data/runtime/risk_policy_overrides.json changed from its manifest bytes to a2b9f5c69f8e3ed4c915d2f52fcef6b4f2a992e75e663c49297a7ac0f35aab44.
findings_requiring_action.verified: root-caused, and the report was precise. The persisted policy was written in text mode, so every save translated \n to CRLF on Windows and re-drifted the file. The tree carried the drifted CRLF form (00bae30979ea63638def84b6829d301e294cdb003cac19096489956a173ed1e8); the Phase131 packaging manifest MANIFEST_SHA256_PHASE131.txt pins the authentic form as a2b9f5c6... (LF), which is exactly the hash the audit observed on a platform with LF conventions. Additionally, 13 sealed research artifacts are rebuilt in place by their change-detector tests (research/phase11g_*/readiness|feasibility|trigger, research/results/phase3{3,5,6,7}_*, phase48_*): byte-identical on the build platform, newline-dependent elsewhere.
repairs: data/runtime/risk_policy_overrides.json restored byte-for-byte to its authentic Phase131 LF form (a2b9f5c6...)
core/risk/trading_policy.py persistence writes newline=\n explicitly: identical policy state now serialises to identical bytes on every platform
tests/test_phase158_snapshot_neutrality.py pins the authentic bytes and the platform-independent persistence

tests/conftest.py installs a session snapshot guard: every covered file is verified against BUILD_MANIFEST.sha256 at session start; a known-rebuilt watchlist is checked and restored byte-exactly after every test; the whole covered set is swept and restored every 50 tests and at session end; SNAPSHOT_GUARD_RESTORED / SNAPSHOT_GUARD_SUMMARY lines record every event; a non-pristine start or a test-added file fails the session
findings_requiring_action.residual: on platforms whose newline conventions differ from the recorded convention, the sealed builders still produce different bytes in-run; the guard restores the recorded bytes after each test so the tree stays pristine, but the sealed change-detector tests themselves (e.g. tests/test_researcher_11g_u.py test_rerun_byte_identical) fail there. Those builders embed their own file hash in their artifacts (code_hash), so editing them would invalidate the sealed bytes; this is a recorded limitation of running outside the canonical Windows / Python 3.12.10 environment, not of the shipped bytes.

findings_requiring_action.as_reported: BUILD_MANIFEST.sha256 was CRLF (198,894 bytes; LF form 197,046); regenerating it byte-for-byte on a platform with LF conventions disagrees by line endings.
findings_requiring_action.verified: reproduced: the revision-1 manifest had 1,848 CRLF line endings and 0 bare LF bytes.
repairs: scripts/generate_manifest.py writes the manifest with newline=\n and writes UTF-8 bytes to stdout, so file and stdout regeneration are byte-exact on every platform
BUILD_MANIFEST.sha256 is regenerated in LF form
tests/test_phase158_manifest_contract.py asserts the file bytes equal a fresh generation and adds a subprocess end-to-end check (generate_manifest.py --root . stdout == the shipped bytes)

findings_dispositioned_without_code_chan.as_reported: the digest re-certification cannot reach the recorded canonical digest (c52e648c...) and is consistent with the documented blocker.
findings_dispositioned_without_code_chan.disposition: confirmed, no change: reports/PHASE158_BLOCKERS.json BLOCK-158-01 records exactly this; scripts/recertify_strategy_digest.py returns STATUS: BLOCKED; no digest was re-pinned, and the five change-detector tests remain red on purpose.

findings_dispositioned_without_code_chan.as_reported: the reconstructed dataset equals the first 11,899 rows of the topup once the rows are ordered by time; the stored raw array is not itself time-sorted.
findings_dispositioned_without_code_chan.disposition: confirmed and sharpened. The claim was already qualified ('in ascending time order'); the artifact's disclosure now states that the stored topup array is not itself time-ordered and that the selection is taken over the rows sorted ascending by time, and tests/test_phase158_dataset_reconstruction.py asserts the raw array is unsorted so the sort cannot become an untested accident. The content hash still matches the frozen commitment 4feccebb... exactly.

findings_dispositioned_without_code_chan.as_reported: the audit ran on Linux / Python 3.13.5, not the recorded build environment.
findings_dispositioned_without_code_chan.disposition: recorded, not a defect of the bytes. The canonical environment is recorded in reports/PHASE158_RELEASE_GATES.json verification_environment; item 10 of the prompt asks the auditor to compare its own environment against it explicitly.

audit_environment_limitations.not_a_defect: none of these limitations is counted as a pass or as an archive defect; they are stated so the next audit starts from the full materials.
